output.review_comment:
The fix to the counting boundaries is correct and should stay: the old loop counted `start` and left out `end`. The new code starts the day after `start`, includes `end`, returns 0 when the dates are equal, and returns a negative count when `end` is before `start`. That matches the docstring and fixes most of the failing tests.

The problem is the new weekend-holiday logic (a Saturday holiday removes the Friday before it; a Sunday holiday removes the Monday after it). The docstring rules this out: "Holidays are used exactly as given: a holiday that falls on a Saturday or Sunday removes nothing and is not moved to a nearby weekday." The logic was added only to pass `test_july_fourth_week_2026`. 4 July 2026 is a Saturday, so under the docstring the business days after Monday 29 June up to Monday 6 July are 30 June and 1, 2, 3 and 6 July, which is 5. The test expects 4. The test and the docstring disagree, and the PR resolves that by changing library behaviour without saying so.

Callers supply their own holiday calendars. Any caller who lists only the actual holiday date will now lose a business day they didn't ask to lose, which changes dispatch SLAs. It's an undocumented behaviour change in a patch release, and the PR has no description flagging it.

Please:
(1) Keep the boundary fix and remove the observed-holiday block.
(2) Raise the conflict between the test and the docstring with the teammate and the fulfilment team. Either the test should expect 5, or the spec has really changed. In that case update the docstring and README, bump the version appropriately and tell callers.
(3) Leave that one test failing, or mark it xfail if the teammate agrees, until this is decided.
(4) Add a PR description explaining the change.
